messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: inference-gateway p99 latency breach (2.1s > 1.2s) and streaming stalls detected. Affects streaming start and tail tokens. Auto-paged oncall.

alice (oncall): I’m on it. seeing p95 ~480ms, p99 ~2.1s across region us-west-2. Streaming stall rate up ~6%.

ben (sre): Thanks — are we seeing errors or timeouts upstream? any auth 429s or db errors in logs?

alice (oncall): Logs show a handful of 502s from auth-proxy and increased RTs from configstore. Quick metric pulls: 
```
# prometheus
rate(inference_gateway_request_duration_seconds_bucket{le=\"1\"}[5m]) -> p95 ~0.48s
histogram_quantile(0.99, rate(inference_gateway_request_duration_seconds_bucket[5m])) -> ~2.1
sum(rate(auth_proxy_5xx[5m])) -> slight bump
sum(rate(configstore_fetch_duration_seconds_count[5m])) -> 3x baseline
```

carol (eng-runtime): Could be KV/cache cold start after a recent feature flag rollout? I see a canary flag pushed 14m ago that toggles config cache TTL and calls out to central configstore on misses.

alice (oncall): yep that matches timeline. featureflag service shows large fanout on rollout: "ff/fast-refresh" enabled at 14:03.

dylan (prod): Customer impact: some real-time streaming sessions report long startup and mid-stream stalls. Estimated affected sessions ~3.2% of streaming requests in US-West. No major billing or data loss reported.

ben (sre): Quick mitigation options: 1) Rollback flag (kill-switch), 2) increase auth-proxy rate window, 3) route streaming to dedicated pool. Which is lowest blast radius?

carol (eng-runtime): Rollback flag first — flip back to previous stable. Also enable local config fallback for gateway to avoid per-request fetches. I can flip and push config in 2m.

alice (oncall): doing rollback now. 

ops-bot: @carol executed: POST https://ff-service/api/flags/ff-fast-refresh/actions -> status 200 (rollback)

carol (eng-runtime): rolled back. Enabling local fallback: 
```
# kube exec into gateway config
kubectl -n infra set env deployment/inference-gateway CONFIG_LOCAL_FALLBACK=true
```

alice (oncall): applied local fallback to 3/4 gateway replicas; watching metrics.

ben (sre): also temporarily widening auth-proxy token bucket: 
```
# auth-proxy config
ratelimit.tokens_per_minute = 1200 -> 2400
```

alice (oncall): changed tokens/min on canary auth-proxy. Restarted 2 pods.

incident-bot: note: automatic SLO alert suppressed while mitigation in progress.

alice (oncall): immediate delta: p99 fell from 2.1s -> 1.35s on canaries, overall p99 now ~1.6s. streaming stalls down to ~1.8%. still above target but improving.

dylan (prod): Customer comms: small percentage saw degraded latency. Hold off broad customer notifications — continue mitigation and confirm stability for 30m.

carol (eng-runtime): digging into configstore traces — queries spiking are the join that resolves environment -> feature set for each request. doing quick index suggestion: 
```
ALTER TABLE ff_cache ADD INDEX idx_env_flag (environment_id, flag_id);
```

ben (sre): Can we hotpatch query plan or warm the cache instead of schema change? schema change might be okay but slower. Warm cache by running a bulk fetch of active envs.

carol (eng-runtime): agreed. warming cache now: 
```
# run from ops runbook
python tools/warm_config_cache.py --env us-west-2 --parallel 8
```

alice (oncall): cache warm complete. watch windows: p95 420ms, p99 1.3s. streaming stalls stable ~0.9%.

ben (sre): nice. Next: schedule the DB index patch during quiet window + add telemetry to detect future ff rollout fanouts. Also add guardrail in ff-service to not fanout > X rps.

carol (eng-runtime): will open PR for ff-service guardrail + add rollout slow-start (ramp) to 5% -> 50% -> 100% by default.

dylan (prod): Action items for postmortem:
- root cause: rollout enabled a fast-refresh path which increased configstore fetches & auth-proxy token utilization -> p99 spike and streaming stalls.
- mitigation: rollback flag, local fallback, auth rate widening, cache warm + route canaries.
- customer impact: ~3.2% streaming requests degraded; no data loss; p99 peaked at 2.1s for ~12m; SLA threshold briefly breached.
- follow-ups: index PR, ff guardrail, observability: add metric for per-flag fanout and per-rollout impact.

alice (oncall): preparing handoff — I'll monitor another 20m then hand to ben for overnight. leaving channel notes and runbook pointers.

ben (sre): I'll take after 20m and run the index PR validation steps. please add any remaining logs to the incident doc.

ops-bot: incident updated: status -> mitigated; severity -> Sev2; link -> https://redwood.incidents/4411112222

alice (oncall): final metrics before handoff: p95 410ms, p99 1.25s, streaming stall rate 0.8%. marking mitigated but in monitoring.

ben (sre): acknowledged handoff. leaving runbook: 
- check ff-service rollout queue: /admin/rollouts
- DB slow query list: pg_stat_activity -> filter configstore queries
- if p99 > 1.6s again, revert any recent rollout and scale dedicated streaming pool by +2 nodes.

alice (oncall): thanks team. monitoring tailed to green. handing off. :white_check_mark:
